valuation.method: Forward adjusted EPS x justified P/E. Each case uses FY2027 adjusted EPS (the period an investor at the 2027-11-18 target date is pricing) for NextEra standalone, excluding the pending all-stock Dominion Energy combination, which is expected to close in 2H 2027 and would change the share count and earnings base. Forward P/E is chosen over EV/EBITDA because NEE is a regulated utility plus renewables developer whose earnings are reported as adjusted EPS and whose holding-company debt is already in the share price. Anchors: 2026 adjusted EPS guidance $3.92-4.02 (management targeting the high end; 9M 2026 adjusted EPS $3.47), 2025 base $3.71, company target of 8%+ adjusted EPS CAGR through 2032, and Q3 2026 diluted shares of 2,098 million. Multiples are our judgement against the stock's own forward range and the rate backdrop, not broker targets.

bear.driver: Wind shortfall persists, FPL and renewables earnings growth slows, Dominion approvals and financing raise dilution, and rates pressure utility multiples
bear.assumption: FY2027 adjusted EPS $4.05 (about 3% above the 2026 low end) at 17x

base.driver: Delivery of the 2026 high-end guide and roughly 6% growth into 2027 as FPL rate base and the 36.7 GW backlog come into service, below the 8%+ company path

bull.driver: 8%+ EPS growth on the company path, with backlog conversion and data-center demand supporting a premium multiple

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY2027 EPS of $4.25 the close of $85.12 implies 20.0x (21.2x on the 2026 high-end guide of $4.02). The Yahoo provider aggregate mean of $94 implies 22.1x on base EPS, or FY2027 EPS of about $4.70 at 20x (+10.6%). Named analyst targets were not available on a common basis, so the gap is shown against the provider aggregate only.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $4.25 (5.0% of target, 5.0 percentage points of price return). A $0.10 change in FY2027 EPS at 20x moves it by $2.00 (2.4 pp).
valuation.watch_metric: Adjusted EPS growth against the 8%+ path, with FPL regulatory capital employed growth (9.2% y/y in Q3 2026) and renewables backlog conversion (36.7 GW) as the leading indicators; Dominion approval milestones also matter because they set the timing of the share-count change.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 and full-year 2026 results, expected around late January 2027 based on the prior-year timing (date not yet announced); Virginia and South Carolina Dominion hearings in Nov-Dec 2026 with final orders expected January 2027.

analyst_notes: Named coverage in the last six months is thin: Morgan Stanley's David Arcaro trimmed to $110 from $111 on 14 Oct 2026 while keeping Overweight, and BTIG's Alex Kania raised to $112 from $103 on 24 Apr 2026, before Q3. Other post-Q3 actions are firm-only and not attributed to a named analyst (Mizuho $80 from $95 Neutral on 6 Oct; Jefferies $87 from $94 on 8 Oct; Barclays $79 from $84 on 22 Oct; HSBC $103 from $114 on 22 Oct; BTIG $106 from $105 on 22 Oct; Argus $96 from $102 on 28 Oct; Bernstein SocGen reiterated Outperform $108 on 22 Oct). The provider aggregate of $94 sits about 10% above base, which needs roughly $4.70 of FY2027 EPS at 20x, or about 22x on base EPS; the reasons for most of the post-September cuts were not disclosed in the sources reviewed.
